concept_title_en: Shadow Play: The Free Man's Door
logline_ar: رجلٌ واحد لا يُرى وجهه أبداً، دميةُ ظلٍّ سوداء على ستارة خيال الظلّ، ثيابه من جلدٍ مصبوغ شفّاف تتبدّل مع كل مكانٍ وكل شطر. يحتمل في ثلاثين ثانية ستَّ عشرةَ مشقّة، من كلّاب الحلّاق إلى حبل السفينة. ثم يقف بأفضل ثيابه على بساطتها أمام باب لئيم، فيرفع يده ولا يطرق، ويمضي نحو الضوء، ويُصفق اللئيمُ كوّته، وتسقط قطعته في التراب لا يلتقطها أحد.
director_statement_ar:
القصيدة في بنيتها مسرحُ ظلال: قائمةٌ من ستّ عشرةَ محنة تمرّ كما تمرّ الدُّمى خلف الستارة، ثم تهون كلّها أمام مشهدٍ واحد هو وقفة الحرّ بباب اللئيم. لذلك اخترنا «خيال الظلّ» العربي، الفنّ الذي كتب له ابنُ دانيال المولود في الموصل، وصوّرناه بعمق الكاميرا متعدّدة الطبقات في رسوم الثلاثينيات وبإضاءة النوار الخلفية. ويبقى الأسلوب نفسه حتى آخر إطار، فالحاضر في الخاتمة يُروى بالظلّ أيضاً.

إخفاء الوجه هنا جزءٌ من بنية الفنّ نفسه. الرأس والشعر واللحية واليدان من ورقٍ أسود معتم بلا عين ولا ثقب، والشفتان مطبقتان لا تتحرّكان، لأنّ الصوت راوٍ من خارج الصورة. هويّتك تُعرف من أربع علامات: تاج الشعر المجعّد المقصوص خيوطاً دقيقة، وحدّ اللحية المسنّن، وذراع النظّارة الرفيعة تلمع من الأذن إلى الحاجب دون أن تُرسم أيّ حلقةٍ في موضع العين، والكتفان العريضان. وتُعرف أيضاً من الهيئة: ينحني الرأس في المحن، وأمام الباب ينحني قليلاً بلا أيّ عمل، ثم يستقيم ويرتفع ذقنه حين يدير ظهره للباب وفي الخاتمة.

الثياب وحدها مصنوعة من جلدٍ مصبوغ شفّاف يتوهّج كالزجاج الملوّن، كما كانت دمى خيال الظلّ الحقيقية، وكلّ ثوبٍ لوحٌ واحد مسطّح هو نفسه شكل الجسد، لا يشفّ عن جلدٍ ولا جسد. ولأنّك طلبت ألّا تبقى ثيابك نفسها، فلكلّ مكانٍ ولكلّ شطرٍ ثوبه، بلونٍ وخطٍّ خارجيّ لا يتكرّران:
- ثوبٌ قطني كريمي عند الحلّاق.
- خيشٌ رمادي ممزّق الحاشية وقيدٌ في السجن.
- ثوب نومٍ كتّاني عند النزع.
- ثوبٌ رمليّ بحزامٍ وعباءة على السطح.
- فروةٌ بلون المَغْرة بحافّةٍ صوفية مشعّثة في الثلج.
- مريلةُ دبّاغٍ بأحزمة.
- عُدّةُ صيّادٍ بصدرية فرو.
- ثوبُ فلّاحٍ بلون القشّ.
- ثوبٌ رماديّ ملطّخ بالسخام عند الموقد.
- عباءةٌ مسحوبة على الرأس للخزي.
- بشتُ تاجرٍ باهت.
- عباءةُ مسافرٍ مرقّعة وقدمان حافيتان.
- صدريةُ حمّالٍ خضراء مغلقة حتى العنق.
- أفضل ثيابه على بساطتها أمام الباب الأخير.
- ثيابك أنت في الحاضر كما في صورك: كنزةٌ عنّابية رفيعة الحياكة بياقةٍ عالية، وبنطالٌ أسود عالي الخصر بثنيات.

لونٌ واحد مشبع فقط يكسر السواد والكهرماني، هو العنّابي لون كنزتك، وهو هنا لون الكرامة. يظهر خيطاً على الكُمّ في أول لقطة، ويبقى معقوداً تحت قيد السجن، ثم يصير حزام مريلة، فعقدةً على عمامة الصيّاد، فبطانةً مخبّأة تحت قناع العار، فحاشيةً مهترئة على بشت التاجر، فعصابةً على رأس الحمّال، حتى يتوهّج بطانةً كاملة في بشته القديم أمام الباب. وفي الخاتمة يعود العنّابي إلى أصله: كنزتك أنت في الحاضر، وهي آخر نغمةٍ للكرامة في الفيلم. الكرامة لا تولد عند الباب، إنّها حاضرة في كل محنة.

والبشت الأخير ليس ثوب ثريّ: الرجل باع داره بربع فلس وباع خفّه، فلم يبقَ له إلّا بشتٌ واحد قديم حاشيته الذهبية باهتة مرتوقة بعناية. الكرامة هنا ليست مالاً، بل هيئةٌ يحفظها صاحبها، ولذلك يبدو رجاؤه «نوالاً» من اللئيم صادقاً ومؤلماً.

الباب موتيفٌ متكرّر: باب الزنزانة، ثم الغيمة التي تُطبق على الشمس كما يُغلق باب، ثم باب الدار المبيعة، ثم الباب الأخير وهو أسوأها. وحين تبدأ «أهونُ» تمرّ على الأعمدة ظلالٌ صغيرة لمحنه السابقة، الكلّاب والقضبان والدبّ والحبل، وتتلاشى ضئيلةً أمام ظلّ الباب الهائل: هذه هي المقارنة التي تقوم عليها القصيدة كلّها. والشاعر لم يجعل الأشدّ هو الردّ، بل «الوقفة» نفسها، لذلك يبتلع ظلُّ الباب ظلَّ الرجل وهو واقفٌ لم يطرق بعد، وينحني رأسه لأوّل مرّة بلا أيّ عمل. وعند «نوالاً» تتدلّى من الكوّة قطعةُ نقدٍ على خيط، تمسكها اليدُ المكتنزة ذات خاتم العقيق نفسها التي اشترت داره بربع فلس، فاللئيم واحد. تنزل يده، ومن أوّل إطارٍ في اللقطة التالية نراه قد ابتعد ماشياً نحو الضوء وظهره لنا، وقد طلعت الشمس أمامه فامتدّ ظلّه حتى غطّى الباب، ورأسه يرتفع حتى يستقيم. وعند «نحس» تُصفق الكوّة وتسقط القطعة في التراب ولا يلتقطها أحد، وينغلق الإطار على شقٍّ من الضوء. ثم يتّسع الشقّ فيصير نافذةً عالية مضيئة في غرفةٍ من زماننا، مقصوصةٍ هي أيضاً من ورقٍ أسود: أغصان نبتةٍ متسلّقة تتدلّى من رفٍّ عالٍ، ولوحٌ خشبيّ من شرائح متوازية على الجدار، وطيفٌ باهت لخريطةٍ قديمة للعالم بلا أيّ حرف. تقف أمامها بثيابك أنت، الكنزة العنّابية والبنطال الأسود، وظهرك لنا، ورأسك المنحني يرتفع كما ارتفع رأسه حين أدار ظهره للباب حتى يستقيم، والضوء يتحوّل من الكهرماني الدافئ إلى فضّيّ ناعم. ولا يظهر وجهك أبداً، فالخاتمة من مسرح الظلّ نفسه لا صورةٌ فوتوغرافية: الحرّ هو الحرّ في كل زمان.

العنف كلّه رمزيّ: ظلّ سجّانٍ بحلقة مفاتيح، وظلّ كلّاب على الجدار، وحبلٌ يضرب الشراع ويمرّ ظلّه على ظهر الحمّال المنحني تحت حمله، ووميضٌ أبيض. لا دم ولا جسد يُضرب، والنبرة جليلة مأساوية لا هزل فيها.
style_bible_en:
GLOBAL STYLE: SHADOW-THEATRE CINEMA (paste first in every prompt). Flat 2D hand-cut silhouette animation in the tradition of 1920s cut-out films, staged like Arabic khayal al-zill shadow theatre and filmed with a 1930s multiplane camera. The figure's head, hair, beard, face and hands are opaque black card with intricate filigree scissor-cut edges. Every garment is translucent dyed hide that glows like stained glass in a muted colour, with its own distinct outline, so each costume reads clearly. Each garment is one flat translucent dyed-hide panel that is itself the figure's body shape; no body, skin or limbs ever show through it. Figures stand before glowing backlit layers of translucent parchment, wax and sand on glass. Deep parallax: foreground layers drift fast, the midground slower, the background almost still, with soft haze between layers. The camera glides between the cut-out layers. Figures are seen in side profile, from behind, over the shoulder, or as hands and cast shadows. Hard backlight only, noir chiaroscuro, long cast shadows on walls and floors, velvety ink-black against amber-sepia parchment, every shadow a hard-edged flat shape. Each scene is tinted like a silent-era nitrate print: night-blue for prison and cold, umber for labour, ochre for desert and drought, red-amber for fire, sea-green for the harbour, warm lamp-amber for the finale. Garment colours stay muted within the scene tint. The only saturated accent is deep burgundy on his clothing, under a tenth of the frame until the finale. Fine 35mm grain, subtle gate weave, gentle flicker, soft vignette, slight halation on bright edges. Figures animated on twos with a slightly stepped, hand-cranked cadence, while snow, smoke, sand and dust drift smoothly. Exaggeration lives only in the scale of objects and animals (giant pincers, a colossal bear, a serpent-like hawser), never in comic motion. Keep the lower 40% of every frame calm and dark; all key action in the upper 60%. No borders, no ornament with letters. Flat 2D, not 3D, not CGI, not photoreal.

STYLE LOCK (repeat at the end of every prompt): flat black cut-out silhouettes with translucent dyed-hide garments on glowing parchment; solemn, tragic, never comic; flat 2D, not 3D.

SAFETY TAIL (append after the style lock in every Plan C job): Exactly one man in the flesh; he is fully clothed, his garment covering chest and back. No blood, no wound, no injury; hardship shown only through shadows and objects. The man never speaks; his lips and jaw stay still. No on-screen text, subtitles, letters or numbers.
character_bible_en:
IDENTITY BLOCK (paste verbatim into every prompt; it never names clothing):
THE MAN, identical in every shot: broad-shouldered athletic build; a big crown of thick dark wavy-curly hair cut as fine paper tendrils, always readable in his outline; a short dark beard cut as a jagged edge along the jaw; thin wire glasses seen edge-on: only the straight hairline temple arm glints from ear to brow, plus a tiny sliver of rim just in front of the brow line; no circle or ring is ever drawn on the head, and nothing bright sits where an eye would be. His head and face are solid opaque black with no eyes, no eye hole and no features; he is seen only in side profile against light, from behind, or as hands and a cast shadow; he never turns toward the camera; his lips stay closed and still under the beard and his jaw never moves; the voice is an off-screen narrator.

RULES THAT TRAVEL WITH THE BLOCK:
- HEAD COUNT: Exactly one man in the flesh. Other people appear only as faceless cut-out hands or as cast shadows that look clearly different from him, never with a curly crown. The recurring other person is a plump hand heavy with rings and a large carnelian signet ring (the wretch: the buyer of his house and the hand at the hatch). The companion in L9 is a slighter cast shadow in a tall wound turban with no curls, a water skin on its shoulder. The boot trader is a thin bare hand with no rings. The jailer is only a long cast shadow with a ring of keys. The barber is only a cut-out forearm.
- FACE RULE (state twice in every prompt): his face always falls in solid black shadow; he never turns toward the camera; his mouth is never visible and never opens; the recitation is an off-screen narrator.
- BACK-VIEW RULE: in back or over-the-shoulder shots, name only back-visible markers (the curl crown, broad shoulders, the glasses temple arm glinting behind his ear). Never name the beard in a back view, so the model has no reason to turn his head.
- SHORT FORMS for single-shot prompts: profile = 'THE MAN (broad shoulders; a big crown of thick wavy-curly hair cut as fine paper tendrils; a short beard cut as a jagged edge along the jaw; a hairline glasses temple arm glinting from ear to brow, no ring drawn on the head)'; back view = 'THE MAN (broad shoulders; a big crown of thick wavy-curly hair cut as fine paper tendrils; a hairline glasses temple arm glinting behind his ear)'.
- POSTURE AS IDENTITY: in each hardship his head bows and his back bends. At the final door his head slowly sinks while he waits; when he turns away, and in the closing shot, he rises fully upright, chin level.
- WARDROBE RULE: his clothes change completely at every change of place, to fit the place and the line, and are written inside each shot, never here. Each garment is one flat panel of translucent dyed hide with its own colour and outline, itself the body shape, with no body or skin showing through; it is clearly visible and different from the previous shot. He is always fully clothed, chest and back covered.
- Do not state an age.
color_script:
Ink-black #0B0907 is constant. Deep burgundy #7E1F2D is the single saturated accent: the colour of dignity (karama), present from the first shot and growing to its peak at the door; its final note is his own burgundy turtleneck in the present-day tail.
• 0.00–1.00 (molar, barber's stall): steel night-blue #2E4A63 with one amber oil-lamp hotspot #E8A54B. Cream thobe. Burgundy: a thin cord at the cuff (~1%). The molar is a clean black shape; no red anywhere near the mouth.
• 1.00–2.35 (prison): pure cold blue, barred light shafts. Grey-brown sackcloth. Burgundy: the same cord still knotted beneath the iron cuff.
• 2.35–3.65 (soul drawn out): blue-grey night, one amber lamp, the light-bird pale silver-white.
• 3.65–4.90 (bringing back yesterday): red-orange sunset over sepia rooftops, draining to blue-black on «أمس» at 4.48.
• 4.90–7.35 (cold, the lone beast): the coldest point: night-blue and parchment-white snow. Ochre fleece coat.
• 7.35–9.60 (tannery): muddy umber #3B2A1A under a black sky. Burgundy: one apron strap. The light dies on «شمس» (9.01–9.30).
• 9.60–11.50 (lizard, bear): a small amber campfire in a deep blue night, then the bear as pure ink-black against the moon. Burgundy: a faded cord on the head-cloth.
• 11.50–14.20 (barren land): bleached ochre #D9BF8C / #C8A15A, the brightest and most lifeless stretch; the last green withers to dust.
• 14.20–16.50 (fire, shame): red-amber embers, then dusk umber-grey in the alley. Burgundy: a sliver of lining hidden under the shame-hood.
• 16.50–18.85 (house sold): warm faded sepia; the only glints are the copper quarter-coin and the wretch's carnelian ring. Burgundy: frayed bisht trim (~4%).
• 18.85–21.05 (boot, companion): hot ochre to sunset. At 20.7, with the high strings, the frame starts cooling toward sea-green.
• 21.05–23.35 (hawser): sea-green harbour night #2F5B52 with ink-black. Burgundy: the porter's head-rag (~6%). Full white flash at 23.07.
• 23.35–28.85 (climax): golden dawn amber on parchment flagstones. The door is dead ink-black with dull brass, lit by a hard lamp-glow above it; from 27.5 the risen sun ahead of him has cleared the courtyard wall and the light direction flips, so his shadow falls back across the door. Burgundy at full strength in the lining of his one old bisht (~10–12%); its gold trim is worn and dull, never bright. The light ahead whitens as he walks into it.
• 28.85–29.57 (tail): still flat cut-out, no photograph. The slit of light that ends S20 opens into a tall glowing window in a present-day room of black cut-out silhouettes (pothos vines trailing from a high shelf, a slatted wooden wall panel, the faint outline of an antique world map with no lettering). Warm amber turning to soft silver light. Seen from behind, he wears his own clothes from his photos: a burgundy fine-knit turtleneck and black high-waisted pleated trousers. The burgundy of the turtleneck (~10–12%) is the film's final note of dignity and the only saturated colour in the tail; the typography carries no glow.
Temperature arc: blue → umber/ochre → fire-red → sea-green → gold → silver.

plan_a.master_prompt_en:
STYLE: Flat 2D shadow-theatre cut-out animation, staged like Arabic khayal al-zill and filmed with a 1930s multiplane camera. Head, hair, beard and hands are opaque black card with filigree scissor-cut edges; each garment is one flat panel of translucent dyed hide glowing like stained glass, itself the body shape, with no skin showing through. Backlit parchment layers, deep parallax, hard backlight only, noir chiaroscuro, long flat cast shadows. A silent-era tint per scene; the only saturated accent is deep burgundy on his clothing, peaking at the door. Film grain, soft vignette, figures animated on twos. Keep the lower 40% of every frame calm and dark. Flat 2D, not 3D, not CGI. Vertical 9:16.

REFERENCES: @Audio1 is the rhythmic foundation: an off-screen male narrator reciting over oud, high strings rising from 21 s; cut on its hissing consonants and pauses. [OPTIONAL, delete if not attached: @Image1 defines only the cut-out technique, hide rendering, texture and palette; it contains no person.]

MAIN IDEA: A silhouetted man endures ancient hardships, each in new clothes, then stands at a wretch's towering door, does not knock, and walks away into the light.

THE MAN, identical in every shot: broad-shouldered athletic build; a big crown of thick dark wavy-curly hair cut as fine paper tendrils, always readable in his outline; a short dark beard cut as a jagged edge along the jaw; thin wire glasses seen edge-on: only the straight hairline temple arm glints from ear to brow, plus a tiny sliver of rim just in front of the brow line; no circle or ring is ever drawn on the head, and nothing bright sits where an eye would be. His head and face are solid opaque black with no eyes, no eye hole and no features; he is seen only in side profile against light, from behind, or as hands and a cast shadow; he never turns toward the camera; his lips stay closed and still under the beard and his jaw never moves; the voice is an off-screen narrator. His head bows in hardship, sinks at the door and rises upright as he walks away. His clothes change completely at every change of place, exactly as written. Others are only faceless cut-out hands or curl-less shadows; the recurring one is a plump hand with a large carnelian signet ring.

TIMELINE (nine windows; hard cuts between windows and only where written; each cut changes angle and shot size; the camera does not cut on its own):
0-2s: Stone prison cell, steel-blue. In a grey-brown sackcloth tunic closed at the neck, iron cuffs and a thin burgundy cord at one cuff, he sits in profile; a cut-out forearm hides his mouth while the wall shadow of iron pincers closes and jerks back.
